rules.blocks: a recursive force-delete (rm -rf), which removes a tree with no confirmation and no undo
rules.instead: delete the named paths (rm path/one path/two), or move them to a trash directory you can inspect

rules.blocks: blanket staging (git add -A / git add .), which sweeps up secrets, local state files and unrelated edits
rules.instead: stage the files you changed by name: git add src/thing.py tests/test_thing.py

rules.blocks: a force-push to a protected branch, which rewrites history other people have already pulled
rules.instead: push a branch and open a pull request, or use --force-with-lease on your own branch

rules.blocks: piping a downloaded script straight into a shell, which executes code nobody read
rules.instead: download to a file, read it, then run it: curl -fsSL URL -o install.sh && less install.sh && bash install.sh

allowlist.why: the build cache is generated output, regenerated by every build; this exact path only
